conviction_note: Q2 is pre-announced inside a $1m band so there is no beat available and 100% of the move is the first-ever guide; the guide has to show a gross margin without the 904bp one-time IEEPA tariff refund that produced the 70.3% Q1 headline in a quarter that was still a $12.1m GAAP net loss, and the syndicate bid that absorbed ~1.9m shares through August ended on 1 September - netted against a real positive (the $125.1m term-loan paydown roughly halves interest expense from Q3) and against a stock already -14.9% in 20 days at its 52-week low, which is why the number is -3.5 and not larger.

findings.finding: Reformation's most recent full quarter before the pre-announced one, Q1 2026, was a GAAP NET LOSS of $12.1m, and its headline 70.3% gross margin was inflated by 904 basis points of a one-time IEEPA tariff refund recovering duties expensed in 2025 - so the entire 'profitable DTC' IPO narrative rests on a non-recurring credit, and the 10 September guide is the first time the company must show a margin without it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is one sentence inside a 'Competitive Strengths' bullet in a 300-page S-1, and the sentence disclosing the $(12.1)m net loss is embedded in a bullet titled 'Adjusted EBITDA'. If the market had focused on it the coverage would not read 'Reformation's IPO filing shows profitable DTC is possible' (Retail Dive, https://www.retaildive.com/news/reformation-ipo-profitable-dtc-model-possible/823857/), the wire summary of the company would not be 'FY2025 net income $12.6m', and 8 of 10 analysts would not have initiated on 2026-08-24 at a $19.25 consensus target, 43% above a $13.50 spot. Ex the 904bp credit the Q1 gross margin was 61.3% against FY2025's 60.2% - i.e. no underlying expansion at all - and no published note or article I could find makes that subtraction.
findings.independence: Revolve Group's Q2 (reported 2026-08-04) separately booked a 162bp gross-margin benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/revolve-group-announces-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-302842702.html - confirming the refunds are a sector-wide 2026 one-timer being recognised now and not a run-rate, and that Reformation's 904bp version is 5.6x the size of a comparable DTC peer's. NOTE: this finding and finding 3 and finding 4 all rest on the same S-1/424B4 document cluster and should be collapsed to their largest residual.

findings.finding: The IPO over-allotment option was almost entirely unexercised and this was never announced: the two Form 4s filed 2026-09-03 show the underwriters took only 60,298 shares from the Aflalo Family Trust and 149,596 from Refo SCSp (Permira) against a 2,109,375-share option, exactly 5.008% of each holder's base sale, implying the syndicate exercised only ~11% of the greenshoe and covered roughly 1.9m shares - about 5.8 sessions of the 326k-share average daily volume - by buying stock in the open market through August; that stabilising bid ended on 1 September.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no 8-K and no press release announcing the closing of the over-allotment - EDGAR shows exactly one 8-K since listing (2026-08-03, items 5.03/8.01/9.01) and the company's newsroom carries no such release. Recovering the exercise ratio requires pro-rating two separate 09-03 Form 4s against two separate 07-31 Form 4s and against the 2,109,375-share grant in the prospectus. If the market had this, the withdrawal of ~$27m of syndicate demand would have been written up somewhere and the stock's -4.46% five-day slide since 1 September would have a named cause; instead nothing at all was published. The conservative alternative allocation (shoe pro-rated at 15% of each holder's own sale) still gives only a 33% exercise and ~1.4m shares covered, so the finding survives either reading; I size on the conservative end.
findings.independence: Confirmed by a second, independently-filed Form 4 for a different holder showing the identical 5.008% ratio: Aflalo greenshoe 60,298 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1787117/000110465926105131/tm2624653-1_4seq1.xml against base sale 1,204,029 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1787117/000110465926089201/0001104659-26-089201.txt. Also independently, short interest rose 147.4% to 879,261 shares between 30 July and 14 August, https://www.thecerbatgem.com/2026/08/30/short-interest-in-reformation-inc-nyseref-grows-by-147-4.html - real selling pressure was being absorbed by something during the stabilisation window.

findings.finding: The Q2 result itself carries essentially zero surprise capacity: the 424B4 pre-announced net revenue of $154.0-155.0m, gross profit $102.6-103.4m, net income $11.726-11.999m and adjusted EBITDA $24.9-25.3m for the thirteen weeks ended 2026-06-27 - a range one million dollars wide on $154m - so the classic first-post-IPO 'blowout beat' pop is arithmetically unavailable and the entire move is the first-ever Q3/FY guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Newly-listed companies overwhelmingly beat their first print and pop, and that base rate is what a reader with no baseline history reaches for - the sealed baseline here has n=0 reactions and no option chain, so nothing in the price is stating an expected move at all. This name specifically cannot beat, because it told everyone in July what the quarter would be. If that asymmetry were priced you would not see a $19.25 consensus target set on 2026-08-24 sitting 43% above spot; the sell-side is still underwriting a re-rate that only a guide can deliver. Also note the pre-announced range implies +23.1% to +23.9% revenue growth against Q1 2026's +30.4% - a 6.5pt deceleration that the 'twenty consecutive quarters of double-digit growth' wire framing obscures.
findings.independence: none - this rests on the same prospectus document as findings 1 and 4 and should be collapsed into that source cluster; the analyst-target side is corroborated separately at https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/REF/forecast/

findings.finding: Cutting the other way and genuinely material: 9,478,821 of the 14,062,500 IPO shares were PRIMARY, and the company is applying ~$125.1m of net proceeds to repay term loans that stood at $246.7m at 2026-06-27 - so interest expense roughly halves from Q3 onward, which is the single biggest driver of the gap between Q1's $15.9m adjusted EBITDA and its $(12.1)m net loss, and it means the first guided quarter's below-the-line is structurally better than any quarter in the historicals.
findings.why_not_priced: The popular framing of this deal is a Permira cash-out - Refo SCSp still holds 28.9m shares and 49.2% - and the widely-quoted headline number is the $210.9m 'IPO raise', not the $125.1m of debt retirement. Combined with the permanent removal of the IEEPA tariff drag (which cost FY2025 364bp of gross margin), FY2026 adjusted EBITDA can be guided well above FY2025's $45.0m even with the refund stripped out, which is the plausible route to this print going the other way. If this were fully in the price the stock would not be at a 52-week low with a levered-equity discount still visibly applied.
findings.independence: Sector demand is holding up, which is what this needs to work: URBN reported record Q2 sales on 2026-08-26 with Anthropologie retail comps +6%, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/26/3351678/4732/en/urbn-reports-record-q2-sales-and-profits.html - the closest listed read on the Reformation customer, given after Reformation last spoke on 2026-07-30. Shares the S-1 source with findings 1 and 3.

searched_and_found_nothing: Promotional intensity: the live sale page on 2026-09-10 shows 'up to 70% off' across 1,284 items (https://www.thereformation.com/sale), but Who What Wear's 2025 coverage shows the identical cadence - summer sale starting 12 August, stepping 30% then 50% then 70% into Labor Day (https://www.whowhatwear.com/fashion/shopping/last-chance-reformation-sale-2025 and https://www.whowhatwear.com/fashion/shopping/reformation-half-off-sale-august-2025). Same start date, same terminal depth as last year. NOT a signal, and the 2026-labelled articles describing '30 to 50 to 70' were serving the 2025 pattern.
The 9-14 September flagship NY sample sale (https://260samplesale.com/pages/reformation-flagship-ny) is on the brand's routine clearance cadence and I found no prior-year baseline to call it unusual.

Lock-up early-release provisions: could not extract the Underwriting / Shares Eligible for Future Sale sections of the 424B4 (the fetcher truncates the document at the summary). Third-party sources give only the standard 180 days on 45,013,708 shares (76.2%), expiring ~2027-01-25 - well after this print - and I found no evidence of an earnings-triggered early release, but I could not read the clause itself, so treat this as unresolved rather than clear.

No 8-K naming the 10 September date exists on EDGAR (CIK 0001787117 shows one 8-K only, 2026-08-03, items 5.03/8.01/9.01), and investors.thereformation.com/news-releases returned HTTP 403, so the date remains wire-confirmed only.
No 8-K, S-1 resale registration or press release announcing the over-allotment closing.
No executive departures, no new Form 4 sales beyond the greenshoe mechanics, no Form 3/4 cluster of open-market selling.
https://www.thereformation.com/stores returns 404; could not build an 'opening soon' store count as a forward read on unit growth.

No consensus Q3 or FY2026 EPS/revenue estimate is published anywhere I could reach - MarketBeat carries ratings and targets only - so I could not test directly whether the sell-side has already modelled the post-refund margin step-down.
baseline_tension: There is no skew and no implied move to agree or disagree with, but my net -3.5 cuts squarely against the -14.93% 20-day run-up, which on this stage's own free control (-run_up_20d, positive on 6 of 6 days) would rank REF as a long; I am accepting that fight because the run-up control cannot see the one thing specific to this name - that the quarter is already pre-announced inside a $1m band, so the usual mean-reversion pop has no earnings surprise to fire it and the whole move rests on a first guide that must show a gross margin without the 904bp refund.
